title: Table, graph, axis and roots for y = x^2 - 3x - 6

source.note: Stem taken from the QP PDF (UCLES 2020). Official answers and mark allocation from the MS PDF. The printed grid is not reproduced. All four parts are paper/self-mark.

stem:
This question is 0580/32/M/J/20 Question 9, taken from the official QP.

(a) Complete the table of values for \(y=x^2-3x-6\).

The \(x\)-values are \(-3\), \(-2\), \(-1\), \(0\), \(1\), \(2\), \(3\), \(4\), \(5\), \(6\). The given \(y\)-values are: when \(x=-3\), \(y=12\); when \(x=-1\), \(y=-2\); when \(x=4\), \(y=-2\); when \(x=6\), \(y=12\). The missing values are those for \(x=-2\), \(x=0\), \(x=1\), \(x=2\), \(x=3\) and \(x=5\).

(b) On a grid, draw the graph of \(y=x^2-3x-6\) for \(-3\leqslant x\leqslant 6\).

(c) Write down the equation of the line of symmetry of the graph.

(d) Use your graph to solve the equation \(x^2-3x-6=0\).

steps.name: T1
steps.note: MS: 4, -6, -8, -8, -6, 4; B1 for 2 or 3 correct, B2 for 4 or 5 correct, 3 marks if all six are correct.

steps.name: C
steps.text_tex: (b) Plot the points from the completed table and join them with a smooth symmetrical curve.
steps.note: MS: Correct curve, 4 marks; B3FT for 9 or 10 correctly plotted points, B2FT for 7 or 8, B1FT for 5 or 6.

steps.name: S
steps.note: MS: x=1.5, 1 mark. Official answer (c): x=1.5.

steps.name: R1
steps.text_tex: (d) The smaller root from the graph is \(-1.4\).

steps.name: R2
steps.text_tex: The larger root from the graph is \(4.4\).
